standard_text: Force and Newton’s laws: Force and Motion, Newton’s Laws of Motion, Action and Reaction forces, Inertia of a body, Inertia and mass, Momentum, Force and Acceleration. Elementary idea of conservation of momentum.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 9 Science worksheets for NCERT Chapter 8: balanced and unbalanced forces, inertia, Newton's three laws, F = ma, momentum, impulse, recoil and conservation of momentum. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Action and reaction act on different bodies.
body_html:
How to think about it

An unbalanced force changes the state of rest or motion of an object. Inertia is the tendency to resist such a change, and mass measures it (Newton's first law). The second law says force equals the rate of change of momentum, so F = ma and F = (mv − mu) ÷ t.

The third law says every action has an equal and opposite reaction, acting on a different body. Because of this, the total momentum of colliding or exploding objects stays the same when no outside force acts, which explains the recoil of a gun.

Example

Force on 1,000 kg with a = 2 m/s²?

F = ma

Answer: 2,000 N

Example

20 g bullet at 200 m/s from a 4 kg gun. Recoil?

0.02 × 200 = 4 × V

Answer: 1 m/s

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting to change grams into kilograms.
  • Thinking action and reaction cancel each other.
  • Saying a moving object needs a force to keep moving at constant velocity.

faq.q: Why does a fielder draw his hands back when catching?
faq.a: It makes the time of impact longer, so the force needed to stop the ball is smaller.

faq.q: What is the law of conservation of momentum?
faq.a: The total momentum of two or more objects stays the same if no external force acts on them.

items.q: What does Newton's third law state?
c: to every action there is an equal and opposite reaction
items.e: The forces act on different objects.

items.q: Why do high jumpers land on cushions or sand?
c: to increase the time taken to stop and reduce the force
items.e: The momentum change is the same, but the time is longer.

items.q: What force is needed to give a mass of 500 kg an acceleration of 5 m/s²?
What does Newton's first law state?
c: every action has an equal and opposite reaction
an object stays at rest or in uniform motion unless an unbalanced force acts on it
items.e: It is also called the law of inertia.

items.q: Why is it easier to push an empty cart than a loaded one?
c: the loaded cart has no inertia
the empty cart has more friction
the empty cart has less mass and less inertia
items.e: F = ma: the same force gives more acceleration.

items.q: How does a rocket move upwards?
c: hot gases pushed out backwards push the rocket forward (third law)
items.e: It works even in empty space.

Why do passengers fall forward when a bus stops suddenly?
c: their bodies tend to keep moving because of inertia
items.e: The lower body stops with the bus.

items.q: Which has more inertia?
c: a rubber ball of the same size
items.e: More mass means more inertia.

items.q: What force is needed to give a mass of 1,200 kg an acceleration of 0.5 m/s²?
When a gun is fired, why does it recoil?
c: the bullet pushes back on the gun with an equal and opposite force
items.e: Momentum is conserved.

items.q: A truck and a bicycle move at the same speed. Which has more momentum?
items.e: It has much more mass.
